_comment: Each entry has exactly ONE of:
Menu     - open a submenu (inline items, or a menu_*.json filename)
ClipText - expand a macro template straight to the clipboard (no process runs)
Mixing them is a load-time error rather than a silent precedence rule.
Suspend      - hand the terminal to the command (fzf, vim, lazygit, less).
rwf leaves the alternate screen, the command draws on stderr,
its stdout is captured, and rwf resumes when it exits.
PipeToAction - what to do with the command's stdout: JumpToPath, ExecuteFile,
Path macros: $P active pane, $O other pane, $F cursor file name, $/ native
separator (so "$P$/$F" is the cursor file's full path on every OS).
Marked-file macros are $M<what><how> - what: F name, P full path;
how: S shell form (space-joined, quoted), L list form (newline-joined, raw).
All four fall back to the cursor entry when nothing is marked.
